notes_for_editor: First lighting is unresolved: LF says the light began service in February 1910 (tower finished late 1909); the department's report for the year ended 31 Mar 1910 lists 'Lighthouse established' and its Chief Engineer 'arranged for the completion' of the tower, and the report for the year ended 31 Mar 1911 lists 'completion of the erection' of the tower (work started 1909-10); fiscal years were corrected by the fact-check (corpus year labels are the year the fiscal year ends); the record says 1909. Story states the disagreement. Roster is Lighthouse Friends only (copyrighted compilation; no USLHS data for Canada); checking against the Marine reports' keeper tables was not done because the OCR columns are unreliable. Edward T. Redford is chief wireless operator in the 1942 accounts but also LF's head keeper 1942-49, and Don Weeden is 'head keeper' in LF's list but 'Assistant Keeper' in its text; both unresolved. Shell counts and times for 20 June 1942 differ between sources (stated in text). The 1920 and 1924/1925 Marine volumes were cited by identifier; the 'December 6' quake entry gives no year, so 1918 rests on Lighthouse Friends (which cites the Daily Colonist of 8 Dec 1918, not read). The Daily Colonist cow item and Redford's report are quoted by LF, not read directly. Parks Canada's own page did not render in the reader; its statement was read through HistoricPlaces.ca. Access: 'tower closed' and 'grounds open' come from an undated LF note; the station is staffed, so visitor access should be checked with the Coast Guard. Focal height 123 ft is a conversion of 37.5 m.
